# Route the intake backlog to on-call queues

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service and keeps its runbooks in the `docs` service. You can use both through the MCP servers of the same names.

The intake backlog is every ticket of team `intake` that has the label `needs-routing` and status `open` or `pending`. Route each backlog ticket to one on-call queue, following the current support routing rules in the docs as of now, 2026-09-14 09:00 UTC.

1. Add exactly one comment to each backlog ticket, with the text `Routed to: <queue>`.
2. For each queue that receives at least one ticket, create one handoff ticket:
   - title: `On-call handoff <queue>`
   - team: `<queue>`
   - priority: the highest priority among the tickets routed to that queue (`P1` is the highest)
   - labels: `handoff`
   - body: one line per ticket routed to that queue, in ascending id order, in the form `#<id>`, and nothing else

Do not change the status of any ticket, and do not change, comment on or create any other ticket.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"type": "text", "text": "{\"id\":\"routing-rules\",\"title\":\"Support routing rules\",\"tags\":[\"routing\",\"support\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-03\",\"body\":\"# Support routing rules\\n\\nStatus: current. Revision 2026-08, in force since 2026-08-03. Replaces routing-rules-2025.\\n\\nEvery ticket in the intake backlog goes to exactly one on-call queue. The intake form writes the customer's answers as lines at the top of the ticket body: `Component:`, `Account region:` and `Customer language:`. Only these lines count; the title and the free text are the customer's own words.\\n\\n1. Component. Find the component in the component catalog (doc component-catalog). Names match exactly, ignoring case. A renamed component keeps its old names as aliases in the catalog, and a ticket that names an alias belongs to that row. A ticket without a `Component:` line, or whose component is not in the catalog, goes to `triage-desk`.\\n2. Ownership. The catalog gives the owner at its revision. Doc ownership-changes lists the transfers since then. A transfer applies from 00:00 UTC on its effective date; a transfer with a later effective date than today does not apply yet, and a withdrawn transfer never applies. When several transfers apply to a component, the one with the latest effective date wins.\\n3. Region. Each team runs one on-call queue per region it covers, named `<team>-<region>`, with region `amer`, `emea` or `apac`. The team page (doc team-<team>) lists the team's queues. By default the region is the account region.\\n4. Language. When the customer language is one of the following, the region that covers it replaces the account region. The language is the part of the tag before the first `-` (`pt-BR` is `pt`).\\n- `es`, `pt`: amer\\n- `de`, `fr`, `it`: emea\\n- `ja`, `ko`: apac\\nEvery other language, and a ticket without a `Customer language:` line, keeps the account region.\\n5. Data residency. A ticket from an EMEA account about a component flagged `eu-resident` in the catalog goes to the emea queue whatever the language. The flag has no effect on accounts in other regions.\\n6. Missing queue. When the owning team has no queue for the region, the ticket goes to the fallback queue named on the team page.\\n\"}"}

steps.message:
I routed all 34 backlog tickets and created the 14 handoff tickets, one per queue that received a ticket. I didn't change any ticket's status. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

- **Excluded:** 901 (duplicate), 915 (resolved) and 930 (closed) have the `needs-routing` label but aren't `open` or `pending`, so they aren't in the backlog.
- **Routing:** I used the current routing rules (revision 2026-08). I checked each ticket's component against the component catalog and the ownership-changes doc as of 2026-09-14.
- **Comments:** Each backlog ticket has exactly one `Routed to: <queue>` comment.
- **Handoffs:** Each handoff ticket has the highest priority among its tickets and the `handoff` label. The body is the ticket ids in ascending order, one `#<id>` per line.
- **Retries:** Tickets 908 and 910 returned a 403 on the first read, and a retry worked. The create call for `payments-amer` timed out. I retried it with the same idempotency key, and the retry returned the original ticket (946), so there's no duplicate.

| Queue | Tickets | Handoff priority |
|---|---|---|
| payments-amer | 902, 918, 919, 920 | P2 |
| payments-emea | 912, 923, 935 | P1 |
| data-amer | 903 | P2 |
| data-emea | 921, 926, 927, 938 | P1 |
| platform-apac | 904, 933 | P4 |
| platform-emea | 909, 910, 917 | P2 |
| platform-amer | 913 | P1 |
| messaging-emea | 905, 907, 924 | P2 |
| messaging-apac | 906 | P2 |
| identity-amer | 908, 916, 922, 925, 936 | P2 |
| identity-emea | 931 | P3 |
| mobile-amer | 914, 929, 934 | P3 |
| mobile-apac | 932 | P2 |
| triage-desk | 911, 937 | P3 |

- **`triage-desk`:** It has no team page in the docs. I used it because the rules name it for tickets with no component or an unknown one (937 has no component; 911 names `billing-portal`, which isn't in the catalog).
- **Status ids:** The first create call that failed was for `payments-amer`, and the handoff ticket ids run from 946 to 959.
